opening: Your Atmos stack with three components, and choudoufu as the binary. This second act adds a subnet to network. Its id is known only after apply.

pull-request.prompt: Add a second subnet to network; put a worker in it.
pull-request.reply: Opened pull request {pull}. Network adds subnet b. App adds a worker in it, and edge allows the range.

pull-request.status: The workflow runs Atmos's affected plan with dependents

planned.reply: One plan across 3 components. Only one value is unknown: subnet b's id, which app's worker needs.

planned.prompt: Why is app's plan a guess?
planned.reply: With stock Atmos, !terraform.output reads applied state, and subnet b is not applied yet. App would get a default or a mock, or the plan would fail. choudoufu plans the three as one plan, so the worker shows its subnet as known after apply.

planned.prompt: What depends on the new subnet?
planned.reply: Two resources depend on it: app's worker and edge's allowlist.

approved.status: Recording your approval as a review on the pull request

merged.prompt: Merge it. Apply network, app and edge in order, each exactly as I reviewed it.
merged.status: Fetching the stored plans after the merge

applying.status: Deploying network, app and edge from their stored plans

tips.title: Only the binary changes
tips.body: Set the component command to choudoufu and give each component a live block. Nothing else in the repo moves.

tips.title: Stored plans, applied in order
tips.body: Atmos's deploy compares a fresh plan with each stored one before applying it. choudoufu stops any component whose plan has moved away from your review.

applied.reply: Done. Subnet b was created first, and app's worker got its real id when app applied.

applied.prompt: Is that what I signed off on?
applied.reply: Yes. Atmos warned that subnet b's id had changed, because it was unknown when you looked and real by then. choudoufu held everything else to your plan before each component applied.
applied.status: Comparing what ran with the approved plan

applied.reply: Never. choudoufu holds no lock to leave behind, so there is nothing to force-unlock. Each record is written only if it is unchanged since it was read: resource-level locking at the cloud level.

closing: 1 plan across 3 components, and the one you approved is the one deployed.
